title: A1 Fitness
text:
The fitness data come from physical performance tests in the laboratory.
Test phases: p1 (pre), p2 (post), p3 (follow-up). See the study timeline.





Dataset
Content
One row is
Key
Rows
Variables




fittsts
Physical performance tests
Participant and test phase
id, tp
191
41







The dataset name starts with the project code fit.



Code
Meaning




tst
Physical performance tests






Variable names combine the test, the measure, and where needed a statistic, e.g. cmjpmax for the maximal power in the countermovement jump. The most common parts are:







Part
Meaning




cmj, hop, bal, step, stair
Countermovement jump, hopping, balance, gait, stair climbing


iso, mvc
Strength on the IsoMed, maximal voluntary contraction


hr, bp, load, vo2
Heart rate, blood pressure, load, oxygen uptake


train
Training volume


f, p, h, ct, ft, rsi
Force, power, jump height, contact time, flight time, reactive strength index


fv0, range, brakedur, updur
Force at zero velocity, upward movement range, braking duration, upward movement duration


max, rel, delta, total
Maximum, relative to body mass, relative change, sum across zones


eo, z1 to z5
Eyes open, heart rate zones 1 to 5

title: A1 Fitness
text:
Physical performance tests
Dataset fittsts, one row per participant and test phase (key: id, tp). It contains body measures, resting heart rate and blood pressure, balance, gait, stair climbing, strength, summary values of the countermovement jumps, hopping, the exercise test, variables relative to body mass, and the training volume per heart rate zone during the intervention (one value per participant, repeated in each test phase).

title: ProPELL Codebook
text: ProPELL is a 21-week intensive longitudinal study with 75 participants (sport science students). It combines laboratory tests, MRI, saliva samples, online surveys, and recordings in daily life with activity sensors, smartphones, and watches. This site documents the processed datasets, with one codebook per project. This page explains what all codebooks have in common.

title: ProPELL Codebook
text:
Codebooks




Codebook
Project code
Data




A1 Fitness
fit
Physical performance tests in the laboratory


A2 Cortisol

Salivary cortisol after awakening and a morning questionnaire


B1 Effort
eff
Baseline, choice, and interval tasks on a cycle ergometer, with fNIRS


B2 Regulation
reg
Brain data (MRI) and performance in five tasks


B3 Ambulatory Assessment
amb
Physical activity (movisens Move 3) and smartphone surveys (movisensXS) in daily life


Z1 Surveys
svy
Screening, demographics, trait and state questionnaires


Z2 Watch Data
pol
Sleep, Nightly Recharge, daily activity, exercise, and heart rate

title: ProPELL Codebook
text:
Study design

The study started with an online screening, followed by test phases before the training (pre), after the training (post), and at follow-up. Participants also completed weekly surveys. The variable tp gives the test phase or study week and uses the same codes in all codebooks. Not every project measured in every phase.

There was no weekly measurement in week 1, so the weekly codes start at w02. The watch data (Z2) have no test phase because they are collected continuously throughout the study (see Linking datasets).

title: ProPELL Codebook
text:
Dataset names
Every dataset name has seven letters: a project code (three letters), a content code (three letters), and a level code (one letter) that says what one row is. For example, corcare stands for cortisol (cor), cortisol awakening response (car), and one row per event (e). The project codes are listed under Codebooks, the content codes in each codebook. Some projects split the content code into a topic or task and a data type, such as ch (choice task) and p (performance) in effchps.

title: ProPELL Codebook
text:
Variable names
Repeated measurements are stored in rows. A variable has the same name in every test phase, and tp says which test phase a row belongs to.
Questionnaire variables follow the same rules in all projects:



Pattern
Meaning
Example




Scale and two-digit number
Item
bscs01, aff01


Scale
Scale score
bscs


Scale and one letter
Subscale score
proei, affv


Item and d
Free-text detail to that item
consumption01d



All other variables combine building blocks that are explained in each codebook, for example cmjpmax (maximal power in the countermovement jump) in A1.

title: ProPELL Codebook
text:
Linking datasets

Each participant has the same anonymized ID, id, in every dataset that contains IDs. The test phase tp uses the same codes in all codebooks, so id and tp link datasets across projects. Within a project, datasets of different levels share the variables of their keys, for example the exercise ID ed in the watch data.
The watch data (Z2) have no test phase. Use date to link them to the study schedule.
The admission checklist and the demographics (Z1) are not linked to participant IDs for privacy reasons, so they cannot be combined with other datasets.

title: ProPELL Codebook
text:
Reading a codebook
Each codebook has the same structure:

Overview: how the data were collected, which test phases are included, and a table of the project’s datasets. The table shows what one row is, the key (the variables that together identify one row), and the number of rows and variables.
Dataset names and Variable names: the codes used only in this project.
One section per dataset: every variable with its label, details, units, response options, descriptive statistics, and distribution. 

Use the search in the navigation bar to find a variable by its name or label.

aeqAchievement Emotions Questionnaire - Sports and Exercise (AEQ-SE)

DescriptionDistributionStatisticsReference



ItemsValuesScale


Directions: “The following questions examine your emotional experiences during sport and exercise. They are organized into three blocks—your emotions before, during, and after sport and exercise. Please first recall some typical situations in which you were physically active before answering the questions. Here, sport is defined as any form of physical activity performed for its own sake; that is, sport is performed for the purpose of the physical activity itself. This includes both competitive sport and recreational sport. The physical activity is goal-directed. The goals pursued through sport can vary widely, for example striving to improve one’s body or abilities, the desire to improve health, comparing one’s performance with oneself or others in competition, social motives, etc. There are also many different contexts in which sport can take place: outdoors (e.g., jogging or on a soccer field), in a fitness studio, in a yoga studio, alone or with others, etc. Typical physical characteristics during sport may include sweating, accelerated breathing, a faster heartbeat, or muscle fatigue. As diverse as the forms of sport can be, so too are the terms used to describe physical activity in this context. In the following questions, different terms such as “sport,” “training,” or “workout” are used. These terms should be considered synonymous.

Before exercise. Exercise can evoke different emotions. This part of the questionnaire refers to emotions you may experience BEFORE an exercise session. Please read each statement carefully and, using the statements below, indicate how you typically feel before an exercise session.
During exercise. This part of the questionnaire refers to emotions you may experience DURING an exercise session. Using the statements below, please indicate how you typically feel during an exercise session.
After exercise. This part of the questionnaire refers to emotions you may experience AFTER an exercise session. Using the statements below, please indicate how you typically feel after an exercise session.”
